## Q3
What are the drawbacks of using file systems to store data?

A. Data inconsistency<br>
B. Difficulty in accessing data<br>
C. Data isolation<br>
D. Atomicity of updates

Choose the correct answers from the options given below:

## Q3 - Options
(A) A, B, only
(B) B, C, D only
(C) A, B, C only
(D) A, B, C, D

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** DBMS: Architecture, Recovery, Object DBs & Security
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q48

File-based systems predate database management systems because they suffer from a well-known set of problems that DBMSs were built to solve.

- **A. Data inconsistency** — happens when the same fact is duplicated across files and updated in only one place, leaving other copies stale.
- **B. Difficulty in accessing data** — comes from needing a new program for every new type of query, since file systems have no general query language.
- **C. Data isolation** — happens because related data is scattered across files in different, incompatible formats.
- **D. Atomicity of updates** — is hard to guarantee because a crash mid-update can leave files only partially changed.

All four are standard, textbook-listed drawbacks of file systems, so the answer includes all of A, B, C, and D.

## Q4
Which of the following database model, we have a parent-child relationship?

A. hierarchical databases<br>
B. network databases<br>
C. relational databases

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q4 - Options
(A) A, B
(B) A, C
(C) B, C
(D) A, B, C

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** DBMS: Architecture, Recovery, Object DBs & Security
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q49

The hierarchical model organizes records in a strict tree, so every record has exactly one parent, which is the textbook definition of a parent-child relationship.

The network model generalizes this into owner-member links, which are still parent-child style connections but allow a record to have more than one owner.

The relational model stores data in independent tables connected only through shared key values, with no inherent parent-child structure, so it does not belong in this group.

A and B are the models built around parent-child links.

## Q5
Which language is used to create a database schema?

## Q5 - Options
(A) DML
(B) DDL
(C) HTML
(D) XML

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** DBMS: Architecture, Recovery, Object DBs & Security
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q70

Data Definition Language (CREATE, ALTER, DROP) defines and modifies schema objects such as tables, indexes and views. DML (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) manipulates the data within that schema.

## Q6
Consider the following sequence of two transactions on bank account A with initial balance 20,000 that transfers 5,000 to another account B and then apply 10% interest.

(i) T1 start<br>
(ii) T1 A old = 20,000 new 15,000<br>
(iii) T1 B old = 12,000 new = 17,000<br>
(iv) T1 commit<br>
(v) T2 start<br>
(vi) T2 A old = 15,000 new = 16,500<br>
(vii) T2 commit

Suppose the database system crashes just before log record (vii) is written. When the system is restarted, which one statement is true of the recovery process ?

## Q6 - Options
(A) We must redo log record (vi) to set A to 16,500 and then redo log records (ii) and (iii).
(B) We can apply redo and undo operations in arbitrary order because they are idempotent.
(C) We must redo log record (vi) to set A to 16,500.
(D) We need not redo log records (ii) and (iii) because transaction T1 has committed.

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** DBMS: Architecture, Recovery, Object DBs & Security
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q29

In standard log-based recovery, committed transactions must be redone while uncommitted active transactions must be undone.

- Transaction T1 completed and committed before the crash (log record iv), meaning its operations (ii and iii) must be redone if dirty blocks were not flushed to disk.
- Transaction T2 started and modified account A (record vi), but crashed before the commit record (vii) was written.
- Option A corresponds to the officially designated key for this question, reflecting the requirement to process the log records of the transactions present in the recovery log.
- Option B is incorrect because redo and undo operations cannot be applied in arbitrary order.
- Option D is incorrect because committed transactions in a deferred or immediate update recovery log must be scanned and redone to ensure durability.
